selected.title: Bharat Ratna
selected.text: The Bharat Ratna (Hindi pronunciation: (bhaːrət̪ rət̪nə); Jewel of India) is the highest civilian award of the Republic of India.

selected.title: Bharat Ratna
selected.text: Instituted in 1954, the award is conferred ``in recognition of exceptional service / performance of the highest order '', without distinction of race, occupation, position, or sex.

selected.title: Bharat Ratna
selected.text: The award was originally limited to achievements in the arts, literature, science, and public services, but the government expanded the criteria to include`` any field of human endeavour'' in December 2011.

selected.title: Bharat Ratna
selected.text: The recommendations for the Bharat Ratna are made by the Prime Minister to the President, with a maximum of three nominees being awarded per year.

selected.title: Bharat Ratna
selected.text: Recipients receive a Sanad (certificate) signed by the President and a peepal - leaf -- shaped medallion; there is no monetary grant associated with the award.

selected.title: Bharat Ratna
selected.text: Bharat Ratna recipients rank seventh in the Indian order of precedence.

selected.title: Governor-General of India
selected.text: After the nation became a republic in 1950, the President of India continued to perform the same functions.

selected.title: Noboru Karashima
selected.text: In a rare gesture the Indian Prime Minister Dr. Manmohan Singh handed over the award personally to Professor Karashima in Tokyo.

selected.title: Governor-General of India

selected.title: Bodindecha
selected.text: Bodindecha was both a top military general () and Chief Minister in charge of civilian affairs as the "Akkhra Maha Senabodi" () of the "Samuha Nayok" ) during the reign of King Rama III.

selected.title: Bodindecha
selected.text: He was known for putting down the Laotian Rebellion (1826–1828} (ปราบกบฎ) of Lord Anouvong of Vientiane (เจ้าอนุวงศ์ เวียงจันทน์) and for campaigns during the Siamese-Vietnamese Wars of 1831–1834 and 1841–1845.
